title: bug: local-runner vm-control canonicalProjectPath matches /mnt/<d> on the raw string, so a relative or non-normalized WSL project path gets a different VM ledger dir and readDaemonInfo refuses its live daemon
description:
Found by architect-4ae016fb while planning task-ea57601d (the moe-proxy comparableProjectPath fix). scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs canonicalProjectPath (about line 31) is a port of moe-proxy's comparableProjectPath, added by CQ-I03a (task-c0b0775f), and it has the same flaw. It detects the drive-letter and /mnt/<d> forms on the raw trimmed string only.

On WSL that gives two wrong results:
- A relative path, e.g. "." run from /mnt/d/projexts/moes, misses both raw regexes. It goes through path.resolve, and the result "/mnt/d/projexts/moes" is returned unconverted instead of "d:/projexts/moes".
- A non-normalized /mnt path keeps its raw rest, e.g. "/mnt/d/projexts/../projexts/moes" or "/mnt/d//projexts/moes".

Effects:
- ownedLedgerDir (about line 44) hashes the canonical string, so the same project gets a different ~/.moe/runner-state/<hash>/vms ledger dir.
- readDaemonInfo (line 126) compares canonicalProjectPath(info.projectPath) with canonicalProjectPath(projectPath), so it throws unreachable for the project's own live daemon.

Fix shape: mirror whatever rule task-ea57601d lands: resolve or normalize before detecting the special forms, and POSIX-normalize the /mnt rest. That way the proxy and its port agree; ideally a shared test table pins both.

Compatibility, the reason this is its own row: changing the canonical form changes ownedLedgerDir's hash for the inputs that were mis-keyed. An input that is already canonical (an absolute, normalized D:/x, D:\x, /mnt/d/x or POSIX path) must hash to the byte-identical ledger dir it does today, so no existing VM ledger is orphaned.
definitionOfDone: canonicalProjectPath maps a relative path that resolves under /mnt/<d>/..., and a non-normalized /mnt/<d> path (".." or "." segments, doubled or trailing slashes), to the same key as the normalized absolute form. Each case is a test in scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs.

For already-canonical inputs (D:/x, D:\x, /mnt/d/x and a POSIX absolute path), canonicalProjectPath and ownedLedgerDir return results byte-identical to the pre-fix code, pinned as literal expected values in a test.
readDaemonInfo accepts a daemon.json whose projectPath differs from the caller's only by those forms, and still throws unreachable for a different project. Both cases are tested.

implementationPlan.description:
RED TESTS FIRST in scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs (node:test). Reuse its helpers: scratch(t), hash(), rejectsWith(), and VC-L1's env save/restore of MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR/HOME/USERPROFILE. Mirror the proxy fix's rows (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts T1/T2, commit e504a57) so both ports are pinned by the same table.

BEFORE touching vm-control.mjs, compute the compatibility literals from the PRISTINE code. Import scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs from a node one-liner and print:
- canonicalProjectPath for 'D:/x', 'D:\\x', '/mnt/d/x' and '/home/u/x';
- the 32-hex directory name ownedLedgerDir uses for each.
Paste them into the test as STRING LITERALS. Never compute them with createHash at runtime: that tracks the code instead of pinning it.

Tests to add:
- VC-L2 'canonical spellings keep their pre-fix keys and ledger dirs' (DoD 2). With MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR set to a scratch dir:
  - canonicalProjectPath('D:/x'), ('D:\\x') and ('/mnt/d/x') each equal the literal 'd:/x';
  - each ownedLedgerDir equals path.join(state, '<literal hex>', 'vms');
  - off win32 only (its pre-fix value depends on the cwd drive): '/home/u/x' maps to '/home/u/x' and to its own literal-hex dir.
  - This passes on the pristine code by construction, and must still pass after the fix.
- VC-L3 'relative and non-normalized /mnt spellings map to the normalized key' (DoD 1). Skip on win32 with the reason 'a Windows process never has a /mnt cwd'. Use `t.mock.method(process, 'cwd', () => '/mnt/d/x')`; node:path's resolve reads process.cwd() at call time.
  - Each of ['.', '/mnt/d/x/.', '/mnt/d/x/sub/..', '/mnt/d//x', 'sub/..', '/mnt/d/x/./', '/mnt/d/x/', '/mnt/d/x', 'D:\\x'] maps to 'd:/x'. Assert the [input, output] pairs, so a failure names the input.
  - 'sub' maps to 'd:/x/sub' and '..' to 'd:'.
  - ownedLedgerDir('.') and ownedLedgerDir('/mnt/d//x') both equal ownedLedgerDir('D:/x'): the same ledger dir.
- VC-L4 'on win32 a raw /mnt path is posix-normalized before mapping' (DoD 1). Use a stand-in when not on win32, exactly as the proxy's onWin32 helper does:
  - set process.platform to 'win32' with Object.defineProperty({ value: 'win32', configurable: true }) and restore the saved descriptor in finally/t.after;
  - `t.mock.method(path, 'resolve', (...p) => path.win32.resolve('C:\\work', ...p))`. vm-control imports the same node:path default object.
  - On real win32, run it directly.
  - Rows ['/mnt/d/x/sub/..', '/mnt/d/x/./', '/mnt/d//x', 'D:\\x'] map to 'd:/x', and '/mnt/d/x/sub/../..' maps to 'd:'.
- VC-M2 'readDaemonInfo accepts this project's daemon.json in another spelling and still refuses another project' (DoD 3). Skip on win32, as VC-L3 does.
  - Fixture: a scratch dir T holding .moe/daemon.json. Run `process.chdir(T)` and restore the original cwd in t.after; the relative caller path '.' then reads T's file through the OS cwd. THEN mock process.cwd to '/mnt/d/x', so canonicalization sees the WSL spelling.
  - For projectPath in ['/mnt/d/x', 'D:\\x', '/mnt/d//x/', '/mnt/d/x/sub/..'], with good = { port: 9876, pid: 1, startedAt: 'x', projectPath }: readDaemonInfo('.') deep-equals { port: 9876 }.
  - For '/mnt/d/y' and '/mnt/c/x': rejectsWith(readDaemonInfo('.'), 'DAEMON_UNREACHABLE').

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs`. VC-L3, VC-L4 and VC-M2's accept rows must FAIL on the pristine code: '.' stays '/mnt/d/x', '/mnt/d//x' becomes 'd://x', and '/mnt/d/x/sub/..' keeps its '..'. VC-L2 and every existing test must pass. Paste the red output into the step note.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW of this diff. Check and note each item:
- Diff vm-control's canonicalProjectPath against the proxy's comparableProjectPath and the daemon's index.ts twin line by line. They must agree on every branch, including '/mnt/d' with no rest, and '/mnt/D/x', which lowercases to 'd:/x'.
- Hostile input: '  ' (ownedLedgerDir refuses it first); control characters; a 64 KiB string; and '/mnt/d/../../etc', which resolve maps to '/etc', not a drive key.
- Does any caller compare a canonical key against a STORED one that was computed by the old code? Grep canonicalProjectPath and ownedLedgerDir callers.
- A ledger dir written under an old mis-keyed hash is now orphaned for that spelling only; the canonical spelling's dir is untouched (VC-L2). Note that residual.
- The tests restore process.platform, cwd and the mocks on every path, including a throw.
- The suite is still not in CI. task-b8b8faba lists it as a residual; say so in the summary.
- The diff stays far under the 400 net-LOC review cap.
